cases.translation: He knocked them out of me over Pushkin.
cases.explain: The preposition «за» in the sense of 'because of / over' takes the accusative; Пушкин is animate, so its accusative copies the genitive form Пушкина.

cases.sentence: Ты ближе к делу, ближе к передним ___.
cases.translation: Get to the point, get closer to the front teeth.
cases.explain: The preposition «к» always governs the dative, so the plural зубы becomes зубам.

cases.translation: And I didn't see any negroes there!
cases.explain: The object of a negated verb («не видел») goes into the genitive, and «никаких» reinforces the negation.

cases.sentence: Негры в ___ живут, а не в Сибири!
cases.translation: Negroes live in the States, not in Siberia!
cases.explain: «В» answering «где?» (location, not direction) requires the prepositional: в Штатах, just like в Сибири in the same sentence.

cases.sentence: Так он там и питался почти полгода: акынами и ___.
cases.translation: So that is what he fed on there for almost half a year: on akyns and saxaul.
cases.explain: The verb «питаться» takes what you feed on in the instrumental, which is why акынами and саксаулом both stand in that case.

cases.translation: All of Europe shared my bewilderment.
cases.explain: Европа is the subject doing the sharing, so it stays nominative even though Russian word order puts it after the verb; «недоумение» is the accusative object.

cases.sentence: Схватил меня, проломил мне ___ и уехал во Владимир-на-Клязьме.
cases.translation: He grabbed me, cracked my skull open and left for Vladimir-on-Klyazma.
cases.explain: «Череп» is the direct object of the transitive verb «проломил», so it takes the accusative; being inanimate, that form looks like the nominative.
The preposition «от», naming the cause of a reaction, always governs the genitive: от смеха.

reading.ru: Он мне их выбил за Пушкина.
reading.question: Why does the toothless woman say she lost her four front teeth?
options: Her man knocked them out over Pushkin
She fell off a horse near Orleans
A dentist in Rostov pulled them out
She never says how she lost them
reading.correct: Her man knocked them out over Pushkin
reading.explain: She sits down with the drinkers precisely to tell how her head was split and her front teeth knocked out on account of Pushkin.

reading.ru: Я женщина грамотная, а вот хожу без зубов.
reading.question: How does the woman describe herself when she shows the gap in her teeth?
options: As a literate woman who nevertheless goes about toothless
As an illiterate peasant who never read a line
As a former dentist fallen on hard times
reading.correct: As a literate woman who nevertheless goes about toothless
reading.explain: She contrasts her being an educated, literate woman with the fact that she walks around with four teeth missing.

reading.question: What does the woman say her whole story began with?
reading.explain: She opens her account by saying that everything started with Pushkin — the komsomol organiser Yevtyushkin courted her by quoting his verse.

reading.question: Whom does the woman compare herself to?
reading.explain: Instead of tending cows and reaping corn, Joan rode off to Orleans looking for trouble — and the woman says she does exactly the same.

reading.question: How does the woman describe the reaction to Yevtyushkin's departure for Vladimir-on-Klyazma?
options: She says all of Europe shared her bewilderment
She says nobody in the village noticed
She says her grandmother explained it to her at once
She says everyone laughed at her
reading.correct: She says all of Europe shared her bewilderment
reading.explain: Nobody could say why or to whom he had gone, and she inflates her puzzlement to the scale of a continent.

reading.question: What happened a month after Yevtyushkin drove off?
options: He sent her a letter from Rostov
She went after him to Vladimir
reading.explain: He returned a month later, and it was on that return that he knocked out her four front teeth.

reading.question: How did the other drinkers react to the woman's story?
options: They wept with pity for her
They fell asleep one by one
reading.explain: Far from being moved, the whole compartment is helpless with laughter at her tale.

reading.ru: Всех доконала, главное, эта глухонемая бабушка.
reading.question: Which detail of the story finished the listeners off completely?
options: The six months in the hayloft
reading.explain: The grandmother who is deaf and dumb yet speaks from the stove about the search for one's 'self' is what undoes them.

reading.ru: Или в Сибири, или в Средней Азии.
reading.question: Where does the woman suppose Yevtyushkin is now?
options: Either in Siberia or in Central Asia
reading.correct: Either in Siberia or in Central Asia
reading.explain: Her logic is that if he reached Rostov alive he is in Central Asia, and if he died on the way he is in Siberia.

reading.ru: В Средней Азии не умрешь, в Средней Азии можно прожить.
reading.question: What is Venichka's verdict on Central Asia?
options: You will not die there — a person can get by
Only negroes manage to live there
There is plenty to drink there
reading.correct: You will not die there — a person can get by
reading.explain: He backs her guess up: there is nothing to drink in Central Asia, but there is food enough to live on.

reading.ru: Так он там и питался почти полгода: акынами и саксаулом.
reading.question: What does Venichka say his friend Tikhonov lived on in Central Asia?
reading.explain: The joke is that an akyn is a bard and saxaul a desert shrub, yet Venichka lists them as groceries — and Tikhonov came back plump.

reading.ru: В Сибири вообще никто не живет, одни только негры живут.
reading.question: Who, according to Venichka, lives in Siberia?
options: Everyone who fails to reach Rostov
reading.explain: He insists Siberia is uninhabited except by negroes, who get no supplies and hang themselves on the towels sent from Zhitomir.

reading.ru: Негры в Штатах живут, а не в Сибири!
reading.question: What does the Decembrist object to in Venichka's account of Siberia?
options: That negroes live in the States, not in Siberia
That nobody could live on saxaul
That there is nothing to drink in Siberia
reading.correct: That negroes live in the States, not in Siberia
reading.explain: The Decembrist wakes up at the word 'negroes' and corrects the geography, which sets up Venichka's next claim.

reading.ru: И не видел там никаких негров!
reading.question: What does Venichka claim about his own visit to the States?
options: That he did not see a single negro there
That he never actually went to the States
That he saw nothing but negroes
That he lived in Harlem for half a year
reading.correct: That he did not see a single negro there
reading.explain: He answers the Decembrist by saying he has been to the States and saw not one negro — the mirror image of his Siberia.

reading.ru: Максим Горький не только о бабах писал, он писал и о Родине.
reading.question: What does Venichka remind old Mitrich about Maxim Gorky?
options: That Gorky wrote about the Motherland as well as about women
That Gorky never wrote about the Motherland at all
That Gorky spent his life in the States
That Gorky was born in Zhitomir
reading.correct: That Gorky wrote about the Motherland as well as about women
reading.explain: He tells Mitrich not to forget the old Motherland and prompts him to recall what Gorky wrote about her.

reading.ru: Это про бабушку, а совсем не про Родину!..
reading.question: How does the black-moustached man judge the line of Gorky that Mitrich recites?
options: It is about a grandmother, not about the Motherland
It is the finest thing ever written about the Motherland
It was not written by Gorky at all
reading.correct: It is about a grandmother, not about the Motherland
reading.explain: Mitrich weeps out the line about going deeper into the forest with his grandmother, and the black-moustached man rejects it as being about the grandmother instead.

highlight.question: Which sentence reports the words the deaf-mute grandmother spoke from the stove?
sentences: И как-то дико, по-оперному рассмеялся, схватил меня, проломил мне череп и уехал во Владимир-на-Клязьме.
Зачем уехал?
К кому уехал?
Мое недоумение разделяла вся Европа.
А бабушка моя, глухонемая, с печки мне говорит: «Вот видишь, как далеко зашла ты, Дашенька, в поисках своего „я“!»
highlight.explain: Only the last sentence quotes the grandmother's remark about how far Dashenka has gone in the search for her 'self'.

highlight.question: Which sentence says what Yevtyushkin did without saying a single word?
sentences: Да!
А через месяц он вернулся!
А я в это время пьяная была в дым, я как увидела его, упала на стол, засмеялась, засучила ногами: «Ага! – закричала. – Умотал во Владимир-на-Клязьме! а кто за тебя детишек…»
А он – не говоря ни слова – подошел, выбил мне четыре передних зуба и уехал в Ростов-на-Дону, по путевке комсомола…
highlight.explain: The final sentence is the one in which he silently knocks out her four front teeth and leaves for Rostov-on-Don.

highlight.question: Which sentence gives the condition under which Yevtyushkin would now be in Central Asia?
sentences: – А кто его знает где?
Или в Сибири, или в Средней Азии.
Если он приехал в Ростов и все еще живой, значит он где-нибудь в Средней Азии.
А если до Ростова не доехал и умер, значит в Сибири…
highlight.explain: The third sentence sets the condition — reaching Rostov and still being alive — while the fourth gives the opposite case.

highlight.question: Which sentence names what Tikhonov ate for almost half a year?
sentences: – Верно говоришь, – поддержал я ее.
– В Средней Азии не умрешь, в Средней Азии можно прожить.
Сам я там не был, а вот мой друг Тихонов – был.
Он говорит: идешь, идешь, видишь – кишлак, а в нем кизяками печку топят, и выпить ничего нет, но жратвы зато много: акыны, саксаул…
Так он там и питался почти полгода: акынами и саксаулом.
И ничего – приехал рыхлый и глаза навыкате…
highlight.explain: The fifth sentence states what he actually fed on for six months, while the fourth only describes what a kishlak has in it.

highlight.question: Which sentence says what is delivered to Siberia once a year?
sentences: – А в Сибири – нет, в Сибири не проживешь.
В Сибири вообще никто не живет, одни только негры живут.
Продуктов им туда не завозят, выпить им нечего, не говоря уж «поесть».
Только один раз в год им привозят из Житомира вышитые полотенца – и негры на них вешаются…
highlight.explain: The last sentence names the once-a-year delivery of embroidered towels from Zhitomir.

highlight.question: Which sentence states where negroes actually live, according to the Decembrist?
sentences: – Да что еще за негры? – встрепенулся декабрист, чуть было задремавший.
– Какие в Сибири негры!
Негры в Штатах живут, а не в Сибири!
Вы, допустим, в Сибири были.
А в Штатах вы были?..
highlight.explain: The third sentence is the Decembrist's positive statement of where negroes live; the others only object or ask questions.
